audit_scope.description: Auditing both EL and CL. EIP-7935 covers EL gas limit defaults and block size security boundaries. PeerDAS polynomial commitment sampling covers CL data availability. EIP-7600 (Pectra meta) covers the fork activation for both layers.

judging.severity_measurement: Impact on the entire Ethereum network
judging.poc_requirement_note: All submissions (except informational) must include an executable coded proof of concept at the time of submission

eips: EIP-7594: PeerDAS - Peer Data Availability Sampling
EIP-7823: Set upper bounds for MODEXP
EIP-7918: Blob base fee bounded by execution cost
EIP-7934: RLP Execution Block Size Limit
EIP-7935: Set default gas limit to XX0M
EIP-7951: Precompile for secp256r1 Curve Support

engine_api.description: EL-CL communication via Engine API is authenticated using JWT and considered semi-trusted
engine_api.rationale: Co-located EL and CL clients communicate via authenticated Engine API (JWT). The Engine API is considered a trusted boundary, but data returned by EL may not be fully verified by CL in all cases (e.g., blob data from engine_getBlobsV2 is used without KZG verification). If the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted data may be propagated to the network.
security_implications: Engine API is authenticated via JWT
Some data from EL may be used without full verification by CL
Compromised EL can affect CL behavior
engine_api.note: Vulnerabilities in Engine API implementation are in-scope, but attacks requiring a compromised local EL may be considered conditional or lower severity

local_validator.description: Local validator configuration is under operator control and considered semi-trusted
local_validator.rationale: Local validator configuration is under operator control. Misconfigured or manipulated validator settings could cause incorrect node behavior.
local_validator.note: Configuration issues requiring operator error are typically out-of-scope

p2p_peers.description: P2P network peers are unauthenticated and considered untrusted
p2p_peers.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary protocol messages. All P2P input must be fully validated.
p2p_peers.note: Vulnerabilities exploitable via P2P network are high priority for bug bounty

Critical.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Exploit an EIP/specification or client bug to easily create an infinite amount of ETH which is finalized by the network
Take down the entire network by sending a single malicious on-chain transaction that ends up crashing all clients
Critical.impact: Entire network (>50% validators or all clients)
Critical.attack_vector: Single malicious on-chain transaction or network packet

High.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 33% of the network
Bring down more than 33% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
High.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Medium.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 5% of the network
Bring down more than 5% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Medium.impact: More than 5% of the network (or >1% of validators for slashing)
Medium.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Low.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting at least 0.01% of the network
Bring down more than 0.01% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Low.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Informational.criteria: Observations or recommendations regarding code quality, maintainability, or system architecture that do not present a direct security risk
Informational.validity_requirement: Only applicable if the team decides to implement a change based on the report
notes: Informational issues are valid if they don't lead to a sufficient impact to count as Low or higher and are valuable enough for the client that they decided to implement the change in the code
Issues related to parts under the 'Out of scope' section will not be considered valid
Informational issues won't have duplicates, and only the first one is valid
They also don't qualify for the 1st and 2nd week multipliers, as they apply only to issues in the main pot

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion via large gas transactions under new 60M limit
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks with manipulated gas limits, adversarial worst-case block size construction

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with invalid blob commitments, submit cells with forged KZG proofs, data withholding
Provide invalid cells, proofs, or commitments to disrupt data availability sampling and recovery
Provide incorrect block data, censorship, denial of service

misclassified_entities.reason: Block producer is a local node component (the validator/miner running the EL client), not an external entity. The gas limit configuration is internal to the node operator.
The data availability sampler is an internal CL component that collects cells from the network. The true external entity is the network peer providing the cells, not the sampler itself.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transactions received via P2P gossip from unauthenticated peers. Any node can propagate arbitrary transactions. Full validation of gas limits, signatures, and nonces required. Relevant to EIP-7935 as the new 60M gas limit increases the upper bound for per-transaction gas.

trusted_external_entities.name: Adversarial Block Builder via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation (devp2p new block messages)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious block builders can construct worst-case blocks that maximize serialized size within the 60M gas limit. Blocks received via P2P are untrusted and must be validated for gas limit compliance and size constraints before propagation.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via CL Gossip (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers send blocks via CL gossip. CL must validate block size against the 10 MiB gossip limit. Relevant to EIP-7935 security boundary analysis where worst-case block sizes under 60M gas must stay within gossip limits.

trusted_external_entities.name: Cell Provider via P2P (PeerDAS)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers providing cells, KZG proofs, and commitments for data availability verification. Completely untrusted - all byte lengths, index bounds, BLS group element validity, field element ranges, and KZG proof correctness must be verified. This is the primary trust boundary for PeerDAS.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Producer via Engine API (EL to CL)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The EL provides blob data to the CL via the JWT-authenticated Engine API. While the channel is authenticated, blob content must still be validated (length checks, polynomial encoding correctness). A compromised or buggy EL could provide malformed blob data that, if not validated, could propagate invalid cells to the network.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API (CL to EL)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL sends execution payloads and fork choice updates to the EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. The EL must still validate payload contents (block validity, gas limits, state transitions) even though the channel is authenticated.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit <= block gas limit (60M post-Fusaka), balance sufficiency, and per-transaction gas cap compliance (EIP-7825 if active).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block propagation (devp2p new block messages)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: gas limit field validation, total gas used <= gas limit, block size within acceptable bounds, all transactions individually valid, state root correctness.
Block size must be validated against the 10 MiB CL gossip message size limit before acceptance. Blocks exceeding this limit must be rejected to prevent gossip network disruption.

All inputs must be fully validated: (1) byte length checks for commitments (BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT), proofs (BYTES_PER_PROOF), cells (BYTES_PER_CELL); (2) cell index bounds < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB; (3) BLS group element subgroup checks via deserialization; (4) field element range validation (< BLS_MODULUS); (5) KZG proof verification via batch pairing check. Invalid inputs at any stage must be rejected.

Recovery inputs must be validated: equal-length cell_indices and cells arrays, minimum 50% cell availability (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2), no duplicate indices, ascending order, all indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, each cell BYTES_PER_CELL length. Recovery from adversarially chosen partial cell sets must produce correct results.

Blob data content must be validated: length == BYTES_PER_BLOB, polynomial encoding correctness. Even though the Engine API channel is JWT-authenticated, blob content from EL must be verified before encoding into cells for network distribution.

Execution payload content must be validated: block validity, gas limit compliance with EIP-7935 defaults, state transition correctness. The JWT-authenticated channel does not exempt payload content from validation.

notes: EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER and EXT-DATA-AVAILABILITY-SAMPLER from source subgraphs were reclassified as internal components (see misclassified_entities).
EIP-7600 (Pectra fork meta) had no external entities as it describes internal fork activation logic.
EXT-CELL-PROVIDER-P2P maps to two boundary edges (verification and recovery) as it interacts with two distinct CL interfaces.
